extractedItems.ruleName: Taking Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions
extractedItems.group: Taking Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions
extractedItems.title: Choosing the Correct Relief Point
extractedItems.question: When taking free relief from an abnormal course condition, which point should you choose?

choices.text: The nearest point where there is no interference for stance or swing.
Any point you prefer, as long as it is closer to the hole.
The furthest point from the original ball location.
A spot that is comfortable, even if still interfered by the condition.

extractedItems.explanation: You must choose the nearest point with no interference for your stance or swing, not just any preferred or furthest spot.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen girl golfer, right-handed, standing next to her ball on a fairway, judging where she can take relief from an abnormal condition nearby.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen girl golfer on the fairway considering relief from an abnormal course condition.

extractedItems.ruleName: Taking Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions
extractedItems.group: Taking Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions
extractedItems.title: Relief Location Choices
extractedItems.question: Your ball is blocked by a road. The nearest point of relief puts you in rough, but another spot the same distance away lets you stay on the fairway if you stand partly on the road. Where must you drop the ball?

choices.text: On the fairway, even if part of your stance is still on the road.
In the rough, at the nearest point of full relief with no interference.
Anywhere you want as long as it's the same distance.
On the road to keep the best angle.

extractedItems.explanation: You must drop at the nearest point where there is no interference, even if that puts you in the rough.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen boy golfer, right-handed, identifying the nearest point of relief from a road on a golf hole, with the fairway and rough shown.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen boy choosing nearest point of relief from a road, with fairway and rough visible.

extractedItems.ruleName: Taking Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions
extractedItems.group: Taking Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions
extractedItems.title: What if the nearest point is in a bad lie?
extractedItems.question: If your nearest relief point is in a bush, thick rough or on a steep slope, what can you do?

choices.text: Take relief and play from there, even if it's a tough shot.
Ignore the rules and pick a nicer spot.
Choose not to take relief and play the ball as it lies.
Move the ball to the green for an easier shot.

extractedItems.explanation: You can either take relief at the correct spot, or decide to play the ball as it lies if relief would leave you in a bad spot.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen girl golfer, left-handed, looking at possible relief options from a tough lie in thick rough next to the fairway.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen girl facing a choice between taking relief in thick rough or playing her ball as it lies.

extractedItems.ruleName: Taking Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions
extractedItems.group: Taking Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions
extractedItems.title: No Play Zones in Relief Situations
extractedItems.question: If your ball is in a no play zone or your stance/swing is interfered by one, what must you do?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies and ignore the no play zone.
Move your ball for free relief, you must not play as it lies.
Take a penalty stroke before moving the ball.
Ask your group for permission to play from there.

extractedItems.explanation: You must always take free relief from a no play zone or if it interferes with your swing or stance. You cannot play from that spot.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen boy golfer, left-handed, standing near a staked no play zone and preparing to take relief.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen boy preparing to take relief from a marked no play zone beside the course.

On the road, if that's the best spot for your next shot.
